exposure: In utero bisphenol A (BPA) exposure (0.05 mg/mL and 0.2 mg/mL via drinking water)
outcome: Fetal Hypoxia induced factor-1 alpha (HIF-1a) expression
Risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in later life (inferred)
cohort: Pregnant rats (Rattus norvegicus) were divided into control and bisphenol A (BPA)-exposed groups, and their hearts and those of their fetuses were examined.
finding: In utero BPA exposure significantly increased maternal blood pressure and reduced glycogen content, and in fetuses, it reduced cardiac troponin I expression, redistributed alpha fetoprotein expression, and elevated hypoxia induced factor-1 alpha expression, suggesting an increased risk of cardiovascular disease in later life.
followup_time: At pregnancy day 21 (delivery for fetal outcomes)
gest_age: From pregnancy day 2 till 21 (exposure period); collection at pregnancy day 21
